\begin{proof}
Let
\[
N=10^{10^{10^n}}+10^{10^n}+10^n-1.
\]
Write $n=2^m k$, where $m\ge 0$ and $k$ is positive and odd. Set $D=10^{2^m}+1$. Since $10^{2^m}\equiv -1\pmod D$, for every nonnegative integer $j$,
\[
10^{2^mj}\equiv(-1)^j\pmod D.
\]
Now $10^n$ is divisible by $2^{m+1}$, because $10^n$ is divisible by $2^n$ and $n\ge m+1$. Thus $10^{10^n}\equiv1\pmod D$. Also, since $n=2^mk$,
\[
10^n\equiv(-1)^k=-1\pmod D.
\]
Therefore
\[
N\equiv1+1-1-1\equiv0\pmod D.
\]
Finally, $D>1$ and
\[
N\ge10^{10^n}>10^n+1\ge10^{2^m}+1=D.
\]
Hence $N$ has a proper divisor and is composite, so it is not prime.
\end{proof}
